items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: When did you join Sam Morgan? That was your first job... Sam here, his band... At Sam Morgan, we had to swing to that band

ctx.x: I've heard you talk before years ago about the importance of the rhythm. That is, you have to have that beat on the trombone. Can you tell us about that?

Yeah, that beat. You see, that beat on the trombone. In other words, you see, when you play this language, you can't rush it. If you rush it, you can't make your chord thing good, understand? See, because you rush in those two, see? Now, especially like our band, Sam, like the band he got there now. But our band, this band never played like Sam Morgan band. Because see, Sam had a tempo. He set you to a tempo and that rhythm holds you right there. You never move. See? Because that's a whole background. Under that…
Well, how would they work with Sam Morgan?

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: When I was with Sam Morgan, we had eight pieces in our band

ctx.x: You know, when I used to go up to Tyler's Big Auden in 1945, you weren't even here then, but you were in New York, I guess. I had Joe Avery and, and we were coming up there. I never heard a solo the whole time I was there. Not one solo. The trumpet would take down and that was all.

Well, and now, now I see, you're just switching to the truth. Now you take, now you take, but Lewis, Lewis Armstrong would tell you himself. The time that, when he was, when he was playing, when he was playing here. When he was at the Dixieland bands, there's no trumpet tape, no solo bar himself, or a clarinet, or a trombone. Sometimes the music would call for, sometimes three or four bars solo, something like that. Three or four bars. Some others would take it, you see. But now like, you play a solo, I take one,…
Really? What was Howard playing? Yes. Trumpet.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: Sam Morgan, Isaac Morgan, and the two brothers... Sam was continued Sam was with our band.

ctx.x: Who was in the band then? You had a trumpet player?
Yeah, we had two trumpet players. Sam Morgan, Isaac Morgan, and the two brothers. Mm-hmm.
